summary: Official 'Final Dismissal (Non-Hearable Issue)' letter issued on June 22, 2026, by the State of California Health and Human Services Agency Department of Social Services (CDSS) State Hearings Division under Case No. SHN-XXXXXXXX55. The State Hearings Division dismisses the Patient's appeal regarding the Conlan Reimbursement default on the grounds that the Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) Conlan Reimbursement Unit has a statutory 120-day review period from the April 2, 2026 acknowledgment date to process the claim. This formal state dismissal constitutes the final, complete administrative exhaustion of remedies prior to judicial enforcement in California Superior/Small Claims Court.

STATE OF CALIFORNIA—HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES AGENCY
DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES
State Hearings Division
P.O. Box 944243, MS 9-17-442 Sacramento, CA 94244-2430
PHONE: 800-743-8525 FAX: 1-833-281-0905

Final Dismissal (Non-Hearable Issue)

June 22, 2026
RE: SHN-XXXXXXXX55

For a free interpretation of this letter please call 800-743-8525.

This letter is to let you know that your request for a hearing that you filed on May 03, 2026 has been dismissed.

We considered any information you may have provided about why your appeal should not be dismissed. The reason for dismissal is because it is not the type of issue that can be heard by State Hearings. The specific reason is:

You requested a State Hearing on May 3, 2026, to address the alleged inaction by the Department of Health Care Services Conlan Reimbursement Unit (the Department) on your claim for reimbursement submitted on March 27, 2026, for medications you indicated you paid for out of pocket. On April 2, 2026, the Department acknowledged receipt of your claim and indicated that you would receive written notice within 120 days of whether you could be reimbursed for the claim.

On March 27, 2026, it appears that you also submitted a claim to your Medi-Cal managed care plan, LA Care, concerning your request for reimbursement. The plan opened a grievance concerning your claim, but later advised you that you could seek review by the Department of Managed Health Care (DMHC). It appears that you did file a request for IMR with DMHC and they informed you on April 8, 2026, that pharmacy benefits are not handled by LA Care because pharmacy benefits are handled by Medi-Cal Rx.

You also submitted a letter dated April 20, 2026, from your provider indicating you are under care for a medically supervised medication taper and that interruption in care due to financial barriers can carry clinically significant risks.

On May 7, 2026, a proposed dismissal was granted in your case as no adverse action had been taken on your claim for reimbursement. The Department acknowledged receipt of the claim but indicated that it was in the review process.

On May 8, 2026, you filed an opposition to the proposed dismissal and a reconsideration task was added to your case. You argued that your request for a hearing is based on the Department's inaction not a denial. You argued that there is a clinical risk if there is delay. You argued the delay in reimbursement is a violation of AB 3275.

Pursuant to the Conlan Reimbursement process, the Department has 120 days from the receipt of a beneficiary's complete claim to adjudicate the claim. If the claim is not complete the Department will request additional documents needed to support a complete claim. The 120 day period may not begin until additional documents are received to deem the claim complete. Claims must meet the following
